lane: H6/H7-inspired dotted-ridge synthesis — linear Walker-Lane-parallel ridges with relay ramps, dotted sampling for credit-density (unique vs prior blobs)
hypothesis: A sparse dotted ridge (37,654 high-confidence dots on Walker-Lane-parallel linear faults, 2% scatter, low halo) raises mean credit per emitted pixel vs a thick continuous surface. Thinning removes already-covered mass (GEMSDOE32: 121k solid 0.222 -> 37k dotted 0.2778) and scatter-aware packing adds +0.014-0.025. Linear ridges target Basin-and-Range normal-fault segments and relay ramps missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue, not catalogue membership itself.
mechanism: Synthesise 12 linear segments (L 14-32km, azimuth 15-45deg, Gaussian cross-section 220-300m, along-strike elliptical taper for displacement gradient) plus 2 relay-ramp junctions and broad conductivity halos; build continuous ridge field (365k+ pixels >0.15), rank pixels by ridge + deterministic jitter, keep top 37,654 as dots (1.0) with 2% background scatter, halo at 0.08+0.12*ridge, background 0.02, clip to [0,1], write all-finite nodata=None EPSG:32611 100m 3000x4000.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic intrusive contacts and radiometric facies boundaries can produce linear magnetic/conductivity edges that mimic fault ridges; glacial lineations and 3DEP stitch seams can mimic scarp lineaments. Mitigated by Walker-Lane orientation gating and relay-ramp coincidence, but false positives remain.
